proposal: The Mandate recommends that the administration follow the language of Executive Order 13834 (agencies prioritize reducing waste, cutting costs, improving resilience and mission accomplishment) and direct the Federal Energy Management Program to help agencies follow the law and use energy efficiently and cost-effectively rather than meeting aggressive extra-statutory renewable-energy goals, with a much smaller budget.

status_summary: Executive Order 14148, signed 2025-01-20, revoked in section 2(rr) Executive Order 14057 on federal sustainability, the order that had replaced Executive Order 13834 (a FedCenter page states 14057 revoked 13834). DOE stayed the compliance date of its clean energy rule for new federal buildings and major renovations on 2025-05-05 (to 2026-05-01), again on 2026-04-20 (to 2026-09-01) and again on 2026-09-02 (to 2027-03-01) while it reviews implementation guidance; the notices do not propose repeal. No replacement order restating Executive Order 13834 principles and no change to FEMP's own program or budget was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 was signed and, in section 2(rr), revoked Executive Order 14057 of 2021 on federal sustainability (90 FR 8237, page 8239).

DOE published a final rule staying the compliance date of its clean energy rule for new federal buildings and major renovations (10 CFR parts 433 and 435, subpart B; 90 FR 18911), effective 2025-05-05, from 2025-05-01 to 2026-05-01, pending review of implementation guidance.
DOE published a notification (91 FR 20868) further staying the compliance date of the 10 CFR parts 433 and 435 subpart B provisions to 2026-09-01 while it reviews guidance.

DOE published a notification (91 FR 56371) further staying the compliance date of the 10 CFR parts 433 and 435 subpart B provisions from 2026-09-01 to 2027-03-01 while it reviews implementation guidance.

title: Refocus federal energy management on cost-effective use, not climate targets
uncertainties: The 2026 notices carry titles referring to repeal of fossil fuel restrictions, but their text only stays the compliance date; the intermediate stay of 2026-04-20 is recorded in the timeline. Whether a replacement federal operations order exists, and any FEMP staffing or program change, were not found; the FY2027 budget summary page read did not mention FEMP and FY2026 and FY2027 FEMP requests were not located. Searches run on federalregister.gov, fedcenter.gov and budget summaries. The Federal Register API list of presidential documents since 2025-01-20 (first 20 of 27 results) showed no federal operations or sustainability order; the remaining 7 were not seen.
